scoring._README: score = sum of the components below. Higher = more brief-worthy. Candidates are pre-sorted by score desc; each item's `score_breakdown` shows its parts.
scoring.recency: 0–1h = 2.3 (breaking) · 1–3h = 2.0 (fresh) · then linear decay to 0 by 24h · unknown = 0.5
scoring.signal: AI/tech (or watchlist) keyword hits — match_count capped at 5 × 0.6
scoring.source: outlet authority from trusted-sources.md: primary (company/lab) 2.0 · citation 1.2 · screening 0.5 · other 1.0
scoring.corrob: cross-outlet corroboration — how many outlets ran the same headline (cluster_size − 1, capped 3) × 0.8
scoring.watchlist: watchlist stream only: matched company tier — Tier-1 +1.5 · Tier-2 +0.8

candidates.title: Google unveils Gemini 4 Argon, retaking benchmark lead over OpenAI and Anthropic — but in limited release
candidates.description: Google unveils Gemini 4 Argon, retaking benchmark lead over OpenAI and Anthropic — but in limited release    VentureBeat
candidates.body_text: Google unveils Gemini 4 Argon, retaking benchmark lead over OpenAI and Anthropic — but in limited release Carl Franzen 1:23 pm, PT, September 30, 2026 Credit: VentureBeat made with OpenAI ChatGPT-Images-2.5 Google today announced Gemini 4 Argon, a new frontier AI model that the company says leads rival systems on several enterprise-relevant benchmarks, including long-horizon software engineering, cybersecurity vulnerability remediation, business automation and economic-impact knowledge work. The model is not yet broadly available. Google says Argon is beginning rollout to a set of trusted cyber defenders through its Fairwind Program introduced earlier this month, and that it is participating in the U.S. government’s voluntary pre-release model access process before a wider release. Broad availability is planned “as soon as possible” for developers, enterprises and consumers, starting with paid API customers and Google AI Ultra subscribers, according to an embargoed Google blog post reviewed by VentureBeat. For enterprise buyers, the announcement matters less as a chatbot launch than as a signal that Google is trying to reassert itself in frontier AI after months of pressure from OpenAI and Anthropic. The company is positioning Argon around three areas where enterprises are already spending: software development, professional knowledge work and cybersecurity operations.
